package.A0: Market research, concept and design (PL1–PL3): research report, approved concept, design and brand file.
package.A1: Brand sourcing (P1–P4): an existing brand's or maker's product, approved and quality-checked.
package.A2: Private label development (P1 → PL1–PL7 → P3–P4): a product made under the customer's brand from the concept on; includes A0.
package.B: Logistics and delivery (P5–P6): goods cleared through customs and in the customer's warehouse.
package.C: Listing and market launch (L1–L5): the product live on the chosen platforms and countries.
package.D: End to end: A1 or A2 plus B and C, one contact from idea to a product ready to sell.
package.E: Ongoing management (O1–O3): reorders, listing upkeep, reporting. No project; a reorder opens a reorder project.

project_type.npi: New product: goes through the full gate set of its path.
project_type.variant: A new variant of an existing product (G2 → G5).
project_type.revision: A spec or packaging change after a change request (G2 → G5).
project_type.reorder: A repeat order of an approved product (G3 → G5).

project_path.a_sourcing: Path A, brand sourcing: supplier and sample (P2) for an existing brand's product.
project_path.b_private_label: Path B, private label: from concept to print approval (PL1–PL7) under the customer's brand.

gate_code.G1: Project start (M): brief and feasibility approved.
gate_code.G2: Sample, spec sheet and NPDS approval (M); not passed without a signed spec sheet.
gate_code.G4: Shipment release (internal): PSI passed, documents complete; approved by compliance and quality.
gate_code.G5: Delivery acceptance (M) at the customer's warehouse.
gate_code.PL_G1: Concept and design approval (M), in writing.

document_type.spec_sheet: The maker's product specification, signed and stamped: the product's evidence.
document_type.tech_pack: Design package for the maker: drawings, materials, measurements.
document_type.sample_report: Sample evaluation: how the sample compares with the spec.
document_type.pi: Proforma invoice from the supplier: quantities, prices, terms.
document_type.po: Purchase order sent to the supplier.
document_type.psi_report: Pre-shipment inspection report (AQL), with photos and video.
document_type.test_report: Laboratory test report for the product's compliance.
document_type.sds: Safety data sheet; required for chemicals.
document_type.technical_file: Technical documentation kept for market surveillance.
document_type.label_artwork: Label and packaging print file: dieline, GTIN, warnings.
document_type.packing_list: Packing list of a shipment: cartons, quantities, weights.
document_type.bill_of_lading: Bill of lading (B/L) from the carrier.
document_type.delivery_receipt: Delivery receipt signed at the warehouse; evidence for G5.
document_type.gate_approval: The customer's written approval of a gate (e-mail or e-signature).
document_type.change_request: Change request (CR): a versioned change to spec, design, packaging or price.
document_type.contract: Contract with a customer or supplier (MSA, SOW, NDA).

document_status.signed: Signed, stamped, sent from the official e-mail and dated.
document_status.approved: Accepted; an approved spec sheet must also be signed.
document_status.superseded: Replaced by a newer version; kept, never deleted.

supplier_status.suspended: No new orders until the issue is resolved.

customer_status.paused: Work is on hold for now.
customer_status.closed: Relationship ended; no new project can be opened.

product_status.concept: An idea or concept; not developed yet.
product_status.development: Being developed or sampled with the supplier.
product_status.approved: Sample and spec approved; ready to order.
product_status.ordering: Ordered; in production or on the way.
product_status.archived: No longer used; its GTIN can be given again.

task_status.blocked: Cannot go on until something else is resolved.

purchase_order_status.draft: Being prepared; not sent to the supplier.
purchase_order_status.sent: Sent to the supplier; every required line cites a signed or approved spec sheet (K3).
purchase_order_status.pi_received: The supplier's PI is in and is being checked (S09).
purchase_order_status.pi_approved: All 30 S09 items OK and the figures add up; lines and terms are fixed.
purchase_order_status.deposit_paid: The deposit is paid; production can start.
purchase_order_status.in_production: The supplier is producing the order.
purchase_order_status.ready: Production finished; goods ready for PSI and loading.
purchase_order_status.balance_paid: The balance is paid; per G4, only after an approved PSI.
purchase_order_status.closed: Delivered and settled; nothing left to do.

payment_kind.balance: The rest of the total, after the PSI.
payment_kind.other: Any other payment, e.g. tooling or samples.

shipment_status.booked: The forwarder confirmed the booking (S15 step 4).
shipment_status.loaded: Loaded; the orders and quantities are fixed (S15 step 7).
shipment_status.in_transit: On the way; ETD and ETA are known.
shipment_status.delivered: Delivered to the warehouse; the dispute period runs.
shipment_status.accepted: Fully accepted with a signed delivery receipt (G5 evidence).
shipment_status.disputed: Delivered with reservations or refused: shortage, surplus or damage (S16).
shipment_status.cancelled: Cancelled before loading; kept for the record.

shipment_mode.lcl: Less than container load, shared container.

market_cell_status.candidate: Being assessed in PL1/P1; no decision yet.
market_cell_status.planned: In the L1 plan, approved in writing by the customer, with a date.
market_cell_status.preparing: L2–L3 content and localisation are under way.
market_cell_status.uploaded: L4: uploaded; waiting for the platform's review or activation.
market_cell_status.live: Active and buyable; the S13 pre-launch check passed.
market_cell_status.suppressed: Suppressed, waiting for a category approval or a document request; the open issue is written.
market_cell_status.paused: Waiting for a customer decision or a prerequisite (registration, EPR, VAT).
market_cell_status.stopped: Taken down for good (decision or platform); the reason is written.
market_cell_status.removed: Dropped from the plan (compliance red, no demand, customer decision); the reason is written.

market_compliance.yellow: Possible with a restriction, document or marking; see the note (S12).
market_compliance.red: Not allowed; the cell is not planned.

stock_source.customer_warehouse: Shipped from the customer's own warehouse.
stock_source.3pl: Shipped by a third-party logistics provider.
stock_source.platform: Stored and shipped by the platform (e.g. FBA).
stock_source.pan_eu: Amazon Pan-European FBA spreads the stock across EU countries.

content_status.en_master: The English master set is ready.

incident_family.ol: Shipment and delivery: trucks, appointments, counts, damage, papers, customs, delays.
incident_family.oa: Platform and Amazon: listings removed or suppressed, document requests, account health.
incident_family.ou: Product and compliance: PSI failures, refusals, recalls, labels, certificates.
incident_family.ot: Supplier: unannounced changes, production delays, PI mismatches, silence, price rises.
incident_family.om: Customer: verbal changes, late payments, disputes, no answer.

incident_severity.s1: Critical: goods, money or the account at risk; management at once, the customer within 4 hours.
incident_severity.s2: Major: a date slips or a cost appears; management the same day, the customer the same business day.
incident_severity.s3: Minor: no effect on delivery or cost; reported in the weekly summary.

incident_status.contained: The goods, listing or money are safe; recovery and closure remain.
incident_status.closed: Closed with its root cause, cost and the measure added to the guideline.

incident_party.forwarder: The forwarder or customs broker is involved.

incident_root_cause.document_data: A document or data was wrong or missing.
incident_root_cause.communication: Information did not reach the right party in time.
incident_root_cause.carrier: The carrier or forwarder caused it.
incident_root_cause.platform_regulation: A platform rule or a regulation caused it.

incident_outcome.partial_recovery: Part was recovered; the impact note says what is left.

incident_deadline_kind.supplier_damage: Damage notice to the supplier: 48 hours under the usual PI terms.
incident_deadline_kind.carrier_claim: Claim to the carrier: 7 days by road (CMR), 3 days by sea per the B/L; 7 days is assumed.
incident_deadline_kind.demurrage: The end of the port or detention free days; enter it from the carrier's terms.
incident_deadline_kind.supplier_storage: When the supplier starts charging storage for goods not collected.
incident_deadline_kind.platform_escalation: Wait 48 hours for a platform case before escalating.
incident_deadline_kind.document_request: A platform document request is closed within the business days set by management (5).
incident_deadline_kind.other: Any other deadline; enter its date.

cost_payer.customer: Charged to the customer; needs the customer's written approval.
cost_payer.carrier_insurance: Claimed from the carrier or the insurance.

change_request_status.approved: Approved by your company (and by the customer when a passed [[(M)]] gate is touched); not applied yet.
change_request_status.rejected: Rejected; the decision note says why.
change_request_status.applied: Applied: the affected document has its new version.

change_request_source.supplier: The supplier asked for it or caused it.
change_request_source.regulation: A regulation or a platform rule requires it.

change_request_urgency.urgent: Production or safety is at stake; decided within 24 hours.

change_kind.spec: Size, material, composition, performance or safety; a new spec version, signed again by the maker.
change_kind.packaging: Packaging, label or artwork; PL-G4 again.
change_kind.price: Price or quantity; a new PI and PO version, the customer's price approval (G3).
change_kind.deadline: Ready date, booking or launch date.
change_kind.supplier: Another supplier; a new spec sheet and golden sample.

panel.title: Page guide
panel.no_tasks: Your role has no task on this page; you can read it.
panel.close_card: How do I close this card?

dashboard.purpose: The single screen of the Monday, Wednesday and Friday meetings. Each box counts what is waiting and lists the first records; a row opens its record. Nothing is entered here.

steps.1: Open the project from the row; its Overview shows the gate panel.
steps.2: Add the evidence the gate asks for; (M) gates also need the customer's approval date and document.
steps.3: Pass the gate; the project moves on and the row leaves the box.

close_tasks.title: Clear a late or due task

steps.1: Open the project from the row; the Tasks tab opens.
steps.2: Mark the task done, or give it a new due date with a note.
steps.3: A blocking task holds its gate until it is done.

sign_spec.title: Get a SKU's spec sheet signed

steps.1: Open the customer's row; the product list shows the SKUs without a signed spec sheet.
steps.2: On the product's Documents tab, add the spec sheet with its version and date.
steps.3: Mark it signed once it is signed, stamped and came from the official e-mail.

steps.1: Open the customer's row; the product list opens.
steps.2: On the product's General tab, fill the Compliance section and add the documents S12 asks for.
steps.3: Set the compliance status to complete; the SKU leaves the box.

steps.1: Open the order from the row; its status shows what it waits for.
steps.2: Do the step: send it, check the PI (S09), record the payment or the production note.
steps.3: Use the status button; a step whose conditions are missing is refused with the reason.

steps.1: Open the shipment from the row; check ETD and ETA on Dates.
steps.2: Log each S15 step on Events; update the ETA when it slips.
steps.3: A late shipment usually needs an OL-09 incident; open it on the Incidents page.

steps.1: Open the incident; S1 and S2 need the management notice time first.
steps.2: Keep the log and the deadlines current until the goods, listing or money are safe.
steps.3: Fill the closure (outcome, root cause, preventive action) and close; management closes S1.

steps.1: Open the request; check the old and new values and the impact.
steps.2: If it touches a passed (M) gate, add the customer's written approval first.
steps.3: Approve or reject; once the new document version exists, mark it applied.

steps.1: Open the customer's row; the market matrix opens for that customer.
steps.2: Open a cell and fill what live needs: platform ID, platform SKU, price, currency, stock source.
steps.3: With the content approved (L-G1), move the cell to live.

steps.1: On a tablet or computer, click Edit at the top right; each box gets a handle, an eye and a narrow or wide switch.
steps.2: Drag a box by its handle, or use Move left and Move right in its menu; the eye moves it to Hidden boxes, where a click adds it back at the end.
steps.3: Click Save to keep the layout in this browser for your account; Discard returns to the last saved layout, Reset to default shows every box in the default order.

setting.purpose: The company numbers the rules read: the default deposit, the spec sheet date, the document request time and the incident notice hours. Only management changes them; every change is logged.

steps.1: Find the setting; the row says what it is for.
steps.2: Enter the new value in the format shown.
steps.3: Save; the rules use it from the next write on.

steps.1: Read the setting the message names, e.g. the spec sheet date.
steps.2: Compare it with the record's date or amount.
steps.3: Ask management if the value itself should change.

customer.purpose: Every customer of your company with its contract terms, warehouses, marketplace accounts and brands. Choosing a customer in the top filter narrows every operations list to it.

steps.1: Use Add in the menu; the three-letter code goes into every code of the customer.
steps.2: Fill the commercial model, the packages and the status (C1–C4).
steps.3: Save; the other tabs open.

steps.1: Open the customer, then Warehouses.
steps.2: Enter the address, dock hours and appointment rule as on the S14 card.
steps.3: Shipments take the address from here; it is never typed on a shipment.

steps.1: Open the customer, then Platforms.
steps.2: Pick the platform and the countries the customer sells in.
steps.3: Note our access; account IDs and passwords are never stored (K8).

transfer_customer.title: Transfer a customer to another company or branch

steps.1: Open the customer and use Transfer…; pick the target and Copy or Move.
steps.2: Rehearse, then decide each conflict: link, new code, empty [[GTIN]] or skip.
steps.3: Confirm; download the ID map, and retry the file copy if files are missing.

supplier.purpose: The suppliers your company buys from, with their terms (Incoterm, deposit, damage notice) and contacts. Purchase orders take their defaults from here.

steps.1: Use Add in the menu; enter the code and the country.
steps.2: Fill the terms: default Incoterm, deposit %, damage notice hours.
steps.3: Set the status to approved once the supplier has passed the evaluation.

steps.1: Open the supplier, then Contacts.
steps.2: Enter the role and the official e-mail.
steps.3: A spec sheet counts as official only when it comes from that e-mail.

steps.1: Open the supplier.
steps.2: Open the Purchase orders tab.
steps.3: A row opens the order card.

product.purpose: The product master (S10): one row per SKU with its GTIN, supplier, status, compliance and spec sheet. The list shows at a glance which SKUs lack a signed spec sheet.

steps.1: Use Import on the list and choose the S10 CSV.
steps.2: Read the report: every row with a problem is listed with its reason.
steps.3: Fix those rows and import again; a GTIN used twice is refused.

steps.1: Open the product, then Documents.
steps.2: Add the spec sheet with its version and date; a new version supersedes the old one.
steps.3: Mark it signed once it is signed, stamped and from the official e-mail.

steps.1: Open the product, then Media.
steps.2: Drop the files; the first image becomes the primary image.
steps.3: Change a file's role from its menu.

project.purpose: Projects take a product from brief to delivery and listing. Each gets its gate set from its type, path and packages; a gate passes only with its evidence, and only G2 and G3 block.

steps.1: Use Add in the menu; pick the customer, type, path and packages.
steps.2: Save; the code and the gate set are created.
steps.3: Add the products on the Products tab.

steps.1: On Overview, open the gate in the phase strip.
steps.2: Attach the evidence; (M) gates need the customer's approval date and document.
steps.3: Pass it; the phase moves on and the next checklist appears.

steps.1: Open the incident that forces it first, from the project's Incidents tab.
steps.2: In the gate panel choose Roll back, pick the incident and write the reason.
steps.3: Later passed gates roll back too; pass them again once the issue is solved.

document.purpose: Every document of every record in one list: type, version, status and its link or file. "Is the spec sheet signed?" is answered here, without opening files.

steps.1: Filter by type, status or the linked record.
steps.2: Open the row to see its file or link.
steps.3: Older versions stay as superseded; nothing is deleted.

steps.1: Add it from the record's Documents tab.
steps.2: Upload the file or paste the Drive link.
steps.3: The previous version becomes superseded by itself.

set_status.title: Mark a document signed or approved

steps.1: Open the document.
steps.2: For signed, tick signature, stamp and official e-mail and set the date.
steps.3: Save; gates and orders read the new status at once.

media.purpose: The library of photos, images, PDFs and videos. A file is stored once and linked to any record; a document can point to a file instead of a Drive link.

steps.1: Open the record's Media tab.
steps.2: Drop PNG, JPG, WebP, PDF or MP4 files within the size limit.
steps.3: Add a title and tags in the library.

link.title: Use a file on another record

steps.1: Open that record's Media tab.
steps.2: Choose Pick from the library.
steps.3: A customer's file links only to that customer's records.

steps.1: Unlink it from every record first.
steps.2: Open it in the library and delete it.
steps.3: Only management deletes files.

purchase_order.purpose: Purchase orders to suppliers, from draft to closed: lines with their spec sheet versions, the S09 PI check, payments and production. Lines and terms lock once the PI is approved.

steps.1: Use Add (or New purchase order on a project); pick the customer and the supplier.
steps.2: Check the Incoterm and deposit taken from the supplier, and save.
steps.3: Add the lines, each with a signed or approved spec sheet, then Send.

steps.1: Add the PI document and enter its figures on the PI check tab.
steps.2: Mark the 30 items; a red difference means asking for a corrected PI.
steps.3: Approve the PI; the lines and terms lock.

steps.1: Open Payments and plan the deposit and the balance from the PI.
steps.2: Enter the paid date when the money leaves.
steps.3: Pay the balance only after an approved PSI report (G4).

shipment.purpose: Shipments of a customer's orders to one of its warehouses, from planned to accepted: dates, the S15 event chain, the S16 acceptance and the document checklist.

steps.1: Use Add; pick the customer, the warehouse and the mode.
steps.2: On Orders, link the orders and the quantities of their lines.
steps.3: Move it to booked with the booking confirmation date.

steps.1: Open Events and add an event.
steps.2: Pick the S15 step, who told whom and the channel.
steps.3: Keep the dates on Dates in line with the events.

steps.1: Add the signed delivery receipt on Documents.
steps.2: On Acceptance, record whether the quantities match and any damage.
steps.3: Accept; a shortage or damage makes it disputed, and an incident follows.

market_matrix.purpose: Where each product is sold: one cell per product, platform and country, with its status, compliance, content and listing data (S05). The cells are the single source; the matrix view is derived from them.

add_cells.title: Open cells for a product family

steps.1: Choose Add cells; pick the customer's products, a platform and its countries.
steps.2: Set the priority: 1 same account new country, 2 new platform, 3 new region.
steps.3: Save; existing cells are skipped and new ones start as candidates.

steps.1: Open a cell from the matrix.
steps.2: Set green, yellow or red; yellow and red need a note (S12).
steps.3: A red cell is not planned; remove it with the reason.

steps.1: Move it through planned, preparing and uploaded as the work goes.
steps.2: Fill the platform ID, platform SKU, price, currency and stock source.
steps.3: With the content approved (L-G1), choose Live.

incident.purpose: Incident records (S17): what happened, where, how serious, who owns it, the log of every contact and cost, the deadlines that must not slip, and the closure with its lesson. A gate is rolled back only through an incident.

steps.1: Use Add; pick the customer, the family and the severity (Y10 §4).
steps.2: Write what happened in three sentences, where things are now and what was done at once; write "unknown" rather than guess.
steps.3: Link the record (shipment, order, product, cell or project) and add the first evidence on Media.

keep_log.title: Keep the log and the deadlines

steps.1: Add one log line per fact, call or decision, with its cost and who pays.
steps.2: Add the deadlines that apply; 48-hour, 7-day and document-request dates are calculated.
steps.3: Enter when management and the customer were told.

steps.1: Fill the outcome, the root cause and the preventive action written into the guideline.
steps.2: Move it to closed; management closes S1 incidents.
steps.3: A closed incident's log and deadlines no longer change.

change_request.purpose: Change requests (S08): nothing approved changes without one. Each records the old and new value, why, the impact, the approvals and the new document version it produced.

steps.1: Use Add; pick the customer, the project and the products affected.
steps.2: Write the old and new values word for word, the reason and the affected gate.
steps.3: Choose the kinds of change and the urgency; the decision date follows.

steps.1: Fill the impact: cost and who pays, delay, quality and listing.
steps.2: For a passed (M) gate, add the customer's written approval as a document of the request.
steps.3: Approve, or reject with the decision note.

steps.1: Add the new version of the affected document on its record.
steps.2: Pick that version as the new version on Decision.
steps.3: Mark it applied; the request closes.

S05.short: The market matrix: one cell per product, platform and country, with its status, compliance and listing data.
S05.long: S05 is kept once per customer and grows as products and markets are added; the cross-table view is derived from the cells. Each cell moves through nine statuses, from candidate to live, and a cell with red compliance is removed with its reason. In the panel it is the Market matrix page.

S07.short: The spec sheet: the manufacturer's signed technical sheet of the product it will make.
S07.long: The manufacturer fills it, not your company; unless it comes from the official e-mail, signed, stamped, versioned and dated, it is only a draft. [[G2]] is not passed, and no order or shipment goes ahead, without a signed spec sheet. Every change needs a new version through [[S08]]; the old one is kept as superseded.

S08.short: The change request: nothing approved changes without one.
S08.long: It records the old and new value word for word, the reason, the impact on cost, time, quality and listing, and the decision. A change that touches a passed [[(M)]] gate also needs the customer's written approval. Once applied, every affected document gets a new version; the request's code is CR-customer-year-number.

S09.short: The PI checklist: 30 checks on every supplier proforma invoice before it is approved.
S09.long: Every [[PI]] and every corrected version is checked line by line; the arithmetic is recalculated, never copied. One wrong or missing item sends the PI back to the supplier, and nothing is paid. An approved PI locks the order's lines and terms and is the evidence of [[G3]].

S10.short: The product master: the single source of product data, one row per variant.
S10.long: One variant is one [[SKU]], one [[GTIN]] and one row; a GTIN is checked and never used twice. Orders, the market matrix, listings and labels take their product data from here. In the panel it is the Products page, filled by hand or by importing the S10 CSV.

S11.short: The PSI checklist: what the pre-shipment inspection checks, product by product.
S11.long: Compliance and quality fill it for the product before the inspection, which is done with at least 80% of the goods packed. Each measurement is written next to the spec sheet's value and each defect is classed with a photo. The inspector's pass or fail is not the decision: compliance and quality decide, and the report is the evidence of [[G4]].

S12.short: The compliance document set: the documents each product type needs, per variant.
S12.long: It is filled within three business days after [[G3]] for each model or variant; one file for a family is not enough. Each document is present, missing, or not needed with a reason; an unsigned or undated document does not count. [[G4]] needs zero missing documents.

S13.short: The listing pre-launch check: filled for each platform and country cell before it goes live.
S13.long: A form filled for one country is never copied to another. Any 'no' stops the launch until it is fixed or a change request is opened; compliance and quality sign the documents and the compliance text. A cell does not count as live before the customer's [[L-G1]] approval is recorded.

S14.short: The warehouse delivery card: one card per delivery address, confirmed by the customer.
S14.long: It gives one warehouse's address, dock hours, vehicle limits and appointment rule; contacts are a role and a channel, never a person's details. It is confirmed again before every shipment, and no shipment is planned to a warehouse without one. In the panel it is a customer's Warehouses tab.

S15.short: The shipment notice chain: who tells whom, when and through which channel, for each shipment.
S15.long: It is sent before loading as one e-mail thread to the forwarder, the customs broker, the customer and the warehouse, and every later message stays in it. Anything learnt by phone is written into the thread the same day. In the panel its steps are a shipment's Events.

S16.short: The delivery acceptance form: counts, damage and reservations, signed before the truck leaves.
S16.long: A shortage, surplus or damage is written as a reservation the driver signs; without it a later claim against the carrier is hard. Photos of the pallet labels, the container door and the seal are required. The signed form is the evidence of [[G5]] and the condition for the invoice.

S17.short: The incident record: what happened, its log and deadlines, and the lesson at closure.
S17.long: Whoever sees the incident opens it within 15 minutes and writes 'unknown' rather than guess; the coordinator classes it within 30 minutes. Every contact, decision and cost goes into its log. It is not closed until the preventive measure is written into its guideline ([[Y10]]).

Y10.short: The incident and recovery guideline: what to do in the first hour when something goes wrong.
Y10.long: Every incident follows the same six steps: record, classify, stop and protect, tell, recover, and close with the lesson. It sets the severities [[S1]] to [[S3]] with their notice times, the deadlines that must not slip, and a card for each known incident coded by family, such as [[OL]]-09 for a late shipment. The 'if it goes wrong' sections of the other guidelines point to these cards.

K5.short: Codes are generated by the panel and never changed by hand.
K5.long: A customer has a three-letter code; projects, orders, shipments, change requests and incidents take numbered codes from it, such as PO-THO-2026-001. The counters run per customer and year in the database, so two users never get the same number. An incident's code starts with its family ([[OL]], [[OA]], [[OU]], [[OT]], [[OM]]).

K6.short: Numbers awaiting a management decision are settings, not fixed rules.
K6.long: The default deposit, the spec sheet date, the document request time and the incident notice hours sit on the Settings page. Only management changes them, and every change is logged. The rules read the current value at each save.

K7.short: The panel is written in Turkish and English; process codes stay the same in every language.
K7.long: Screens, hints and guides are written by hand in Turkish and English; the other languages show the English text for now. Codes such as [[G2]], [[S09]] or [[L-G1]] are never translated, so a code means the same thing in every document and conversation.

K8.short: Sensitive data is never stored in the panel.
K8.long: There is no field for bank details, tax or EORI numbers, passwords or platform case numbers. Customer and supplier cards link to a restricted Drive folder instead. Contacts are a role and an official channel, never a personal phone number or e-mail.

A0.long: Package A0 is the research and concept work before a product is developed: market research, an approved concept, design and the brand file. It runs through phases PL1–PL3 and ends with the concept approval [[PL-G1]]. It is part of [[A2]].

A1.long: Package A1 finds an existing brand's or manufacturer's product, gets it approved and checks its quality. It runs through P1–P4 with the gates [[G1]] to [[G4]]: brief, sample and spec sheet, order, inspection.

A2.long: Package A2 develops a product under the customer's own brand from the concept on, with the private label gates [[PL-G1]] to [[PL-G4]] between P1 and P3. It includes [[A0]] and needs a golden sample before mass production.

B.long: Package B brings the goods from the supplier to the customer's warehouse: packing, logistics, customs and delivery (P5–P6). It starts after [[G4]] and ends with the delivery acceptance [[G5]].

C.long: Package C puts the product on sale: content, listings and launch on the chosen platforms and countries (L1–L5). Each platform and country is a cell of the market matrix ([[S05]]); content needs [[L-G1]] before it goes live.

D.long: Package D is the end-to-end offer: [[A1]] or [[A2]], then [[B]] and [[C]], with one contact from the idea to a product ready to sell. Its project carries the gates of all its parts.

E.long: Package E is the ongoing management after launch: reorders, listing upkeep and reporting (O1–O3). It opens no project of its own; each reorder opens a reorder project that starts at [[G3]].

G1.long: The customer approves the brief and the feasibility in writing; sourcing starts only after it. The evidence is the approval e-mail or e-signature.

G2.long: The customer approves the sample, the spec sheet and the NPDS in writing. It is never passed without a signed spec sheet ([[S07]]); in the panel it blocks until every linked product has a signed or approved spec sheet.

G3.long: The customer approves the price, the [[PI]] and the print files in writing before production. In the panel it blocks until one of the project's orders has an approved PI ([[S09]]).

G4.long: An internal gate: the goods are released for shipment once the [[PSI]] has passed and the documents are complete ([[S12]]). Compliance and quality approve it; the balance is not paid before it.

G5.long: The customer accepts the delivery at its warehouse. The signed delivery receipt ([[S16]]) is the evidence and the condition for the invoice.

PL_G1.long: The customer approves the concept and the design in writing at the end of research and concept (PL1–PL2). Brand and product development start only after it.

PL_G2.long: The customer approves the brand and its identity: name, logo, colours and tone (PL3). The packaging and content work builds on it.

PL_G3.long: The customer approves the golden sample, the reference for mass production. Photos and content start from it before production ends, and the [[PSI]] checks the goods against it.

PL_G4.long: The customer approves the packaging artwork before it goes to print (PL6). The artwork carries the [[GTIN]], the warnings and the markings of the target countries.

L_G1.long: The customer approves the listing content in writing before it goes live. A market cell cannot go live without approved content ([[S13]]).

L_G2.long: The customer accepts the closure of the project after launch; the final market matrix ([[S05]]) goes into the delivery file.

M_gate.short: A gate marked (M) needs the customer's written approval.
M_gate.long: The approval comes by e-mail or e-signature and is filed as a document of the gate; a verbal or chat approval is confirmed by e-mail the same day. In the panel an (M) gate passes only with the customer's approval date and document. Changing something a passed (M) gate approved needs a change request with the customer's written approval ([[S08]]).

OL.long: Shipment and delivery incidents have the cards OL-01 to OL-12, from a wrong truck to a refused FBA delivery. Most start at a warehouse or a port; [[S14]], [[S15]] and [[S16]] exist to prevent them.

OA.long: Platform incidents have the cards OA-01 to OA-10: removed or suppressed listings, document requests, [[ASIN]] or [[EAN]] conflicts, account health. A platform case number is never written in the panel ([[K8]]).

OU.long: Product and compliance incidents have the cards OU-01 to OU-06: a failed [[PSI]], a refusal at delivery, a recall, a missing legal label, an invalid test report. A gate that has to be redone is rolled back through an incident like these.

OT.long: Supplier incidents have the cards OT-01 to OT-08: an unannounced spec change, a production delay, a [[PI]] or invoice mismatch, a mould or IP issue, bank detail fraud, no answer, a price rise. The supplier's PI terms set deadlines such as the 48-hour damage notice.

OM.long: Customer incidents have the cards OM-01 to OM-06: a verbal change, a late payment, a refused extra cost, a dispute, no answer, an outside provider or IP issue. A verbal change is written down the same day and handled as a change request ([[S08]]).

S1.long: Goods, money or the account are at risk: damaged or lost goods, goods held at customs, a closed listing or account, a recall, a lost payment. Management is told at once by phone and in writing, the customer within 4 hours. Only management closes an S1 incident.

S2.long: A delivery or launch date slips or an extra cost appears: waiting fees, a second trip, relabelling, a document request. Management is told in writing the same day and the customer the same business day. The incident leaves open only once management has been told.

S3.long: Delivery and cost are not affected: a document correction, a small count difference, a notice. It is reported at the weekly meeting and in the customer's weekly summary.

PI.short: Proforma invoice: the supplier's preliminary invoice with products, prices, totals and terms.
PI.long: The deposit is paid against it, so it is checked with [[S09]] before anything is paid. Only one file version of a PI is valid; a corrected PI is a new version. Its approval is the evidence of [[G3]] and locks the purchase order.

PSI.short: Pre-shipment inspection: the quality check before the goods are loaded.
PSI.long: An outside inspector or a trusted local agent checks the goods against the spec sheet with the AQL standard, using the [[S11]] checklist. The balance is paid only after an approved PSI report, and [[G4]] needs it. A failed PSI is an [[OU]] incident.

ETD.short: Estimated time of departure of a shipment.
ETD.long: The forwarder gives it at booking; it is kept on the shipment's Dates tab. When it slips, the customer is told, and a late shipment usually opens an [[OL]]-09 incident.

ETA.short: Estimated time of arrival at the destination warehouse.
ETA.long: It is updated whenever the forwarder announces a change, and every change is passed on to the customer ([[S15]]). The dashboard lists shipments by their ETA. A shipment does not go in transit without [[ETD]] and ETA.

CMR.short: The consignment note of road transport under the CMR convention.
CMR.long: It travels with every truck shipment, for example from Türkiye to the EU. Damage or a shortage is written on it at delivery; hidden damage is claimed from the carrier within 7 days. A missing or wrong CMR is an [[OL]]-07 incident.

GTIN.short: Global Trade Item Number: the barcode number that identifies a product worldwide.
GTIN.long: It is the general name of [[EAN]], UPC and similar codes: 8, 12, 13 or 14 digits with a check digit, bought from GS1. One variant has one GTIN; the panel checks the digit and refuses a GTIN used by another active product. An archived product's GTIN can be given again.

EAN.short: European Article Number: the 13-digit GTIN printed under the barcode.
EAN.long: Retailers and Amazon need it to open a listing. The same EAN on two different packs is an error that merges listings ([[OA]]-05). In the panel it is entered as the product's [[GTIN]].

ASIN.short: Amazon Standard Identification Number: the 10-character ID of a product page on Amazon.
ASIN.long: Amazon gives it when the listing is opened; several sellers can sell under one ASIN. In the panel it is the platform product ID of an Amazon market cell, needed before the cell goes live ([[S05]]).

SKU.short: Stock keeping unit: the seller's own code for one product variant.
SKU.long: One variant is one SKU and one row of the product master ([[S10]]); it holds no platform or country. A marketplace may have its own platform SKU for the same product, kept on the market cell. A SKU is unique.

system_guide.title: System guide
system_guide.intro: How the panel works and what its codes mean, the same for every role. A dotted code anywhere in the panel opens its entry.

process.title: Process documents
process.intro: The guideline (Y) and template (S) documents of the workflow the panel follows.

rules.title: Panel rules
rules.intro: Decisions of the panel's design (K) that every screen follows.

packages.title: Service packages
packages.intro: What your company sells; a project's gates come from its packages.

gates.title: Gate set
gates.intro: A phase ends at a gate, passed only with its evidence; the next phase does not start before it.

incidents.title: Incident families and severities
incidents.intro: Every incident has a family, which starts its code, and a severity, which sets who is told and when ([[Y10]]).

abbreviations.title: Abbreviations
abbreviations.intro: Trade abbreviations used on the screens.

customer_filter.title: The customer filter
customer_filter.text: The customer chosen in the top bar narrows every operations list and the dashboard to that customer; 'All customers' shows everything your role may see. The choice stays as you move between pages.

cards_tabs.title: Cards and tabs
cards_tabs.text: A row opens its record as a card over the list, with tabs for its parts: general data, lines, documents, media, history. A new record shows its first tab only; the others open once it is saved. The address of a card and tab can be shared as a link.

status_buttons.title: Status buttons
status_buttons.text: A record's status changes only through its status buttons, which offer the moves allowed from the current status. A move whose conditions are missing is refused with the reason, for example a gate without its evidence. Save or discard your edits before changing the status.

document_versions.title: Documents and versions
document_versions.text: A document is a link or a file with a type, a version and a status. A new version supersedes the old one by itself; nothing is deleted, so the history stays readable. Gates, orders and shipments read the status (signed, approved) directly.

branches.title: Company, branches and roles
branches.text: Your company is one tenant: its data is never visible to another company. A company can have branches; pages show the data of the branches checked in the branch picker, and new records go to the branch with the star. What you can do on each page depends on your role.
